# Music in Wolfram Language and WLJS

This tutorial starts with the low-level `Sound` and `SoundNote` expressions used to describe playable audio, then moves to the higher-level `Music*` framework introduced in WL 15. We will build examples from notes and chords to timed layers and multi-voice scores, while keeping every musical object available for inspection and transformation.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Sound[{
	  SoundNote[{"C4", "E4", "G4"}, {0, 1/2}],
	  SoundNote["A4", {1/2, 1}],
	  SoundNote["F4", {1, 3/2}],
	  SoundNote["G4", {3/2, 2}]
	}]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Sound[{SoundNote[{"C4", "E4", "G4"}, {0, 1/2}], SoundNote["A4", {1/2, 1}], SoundNote["F4", {1, 3/2}], SoundNote["G4", {3/2, 2}]}])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/NS0ljgUn6ZBaXpDGBeJwwSb/8ktQ0ZmQFwSAFziZgyhVCuZtAdMGUZAJpBogQB5AISizJzM9LzMkE2ZvJBJdDsQRskCOaQfjMALNwGeSG7iJG7C5iJuQidK/hMwNMAACvpUHK"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

### Listen to the result

Click the output to play it. A `SoundNote` with one pitch describes a single event; a list of pitches in one `SoundNote` starts them simultaneously, which is how a chord is represented. Explicit start and end times make the sequence easy to read and edit.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`SoundNote[{"C3", "E3", "G3"}] // Sound`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Sound[SoundNote[{"C3", "E3", "G3"}]])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/Ng3I5YVy//JLUNGaYep/M4pJgJiDD2RhMuUIod2MA5nUP9w=="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

### Durations

The second argument controls duration when it is a number. Exact values such as `1/4` and `1/2` are convenient for expressing relative rhythm and keeping the timing easy to edit.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`{
	  SoundNote[{"C3", "E3", "G3"}, 1/4],
	  SoundNote[{"A2", "C3", "E3"}, 1/4],
	  SoundNote[{"F2", "A2", "C3"}, 1/4],
	  SoundNote[{"G2", "B2", "D3"}, 1/2]
	} // Sound`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Sound[{SoundNote[{"C3", "E3", "G3"}, 1/4], SoundNote[{"A2", "C3", "E3"}, 1/4], SoundNote[{"F2", "A2", "C3"}, 1/4], SoundNote[{"G2", "B2", "D3"}, 1/2]}])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/NS0ljgUn6ZBaXpDGBeJwwSb/8ktQ0ZmQFwSAFzsZgyhVCuRtDdHEAiaDEksz8vMScTJAlmSBNxJnoaIRqMOUmuhmhGky5ie4Qo5wglAtOE0HCAK6BQmM="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

### Absolute timing

For precise placement, give `SoundNote` a start/end pair `{t0, t1}`. This is useful for layering sustained notes, synchronizing parts, or leaving intentional gaps.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Sound[{
	  SoundNote["C2", {0, 2}],
	  SoundNote[{"C3", "E3", "G3"}, {0, 1}],
	  SoundNote[{"F3", "A3", "C4"}, {1, 2}],
	  SoundNote[{"G3", "B3", "D4"}, {2, 3}]
	}]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Sound[{SoundNote["C2", {0, 2}], SoundNote[{"C3", "E3", "G3"}, {0, 1}], SoundNote[{"F3", "A3", "C4"}, {1, 2}], SoundNote[{"G3", "B3", "D4"}, {2, 3}]}])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/NS0ljgUn6ZBaXpDGBeJwwSb/8ktRgkJCzEUQGpi4TSDNkgoSw6EhjRlYK0W8MplwhlLsxNtMYiTbNDWKMI4RyNkEzjZE0t7lDjHGCUC7opoF4mSBdAMPuN8g="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

### Instruments

The third argument selects the instrument used for playback. The next example assigns a different timbre to each note; the names marked `WLJS only` are provided by the browser-based WLJS audio engine.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Sound[{
	  SoundNote["C5", {0., .4}, "Piano"],
	  SoundNote["D5", {.5, .9}, "Guitar"],
	  SoundNote["E5", {1., 1.4}, "Violin"],
	  SoundNote["F5", {1.5, 1.9}, "Flute"],
	  SoundNote["G5", {2., 2.4}, "Trumpet"],
	  SoundNote["A5", {2.5, 2.9}, "Organ"],
	  SoundNote["B5", {3., 3.4}, "Marimba"],
	  SoundNote["C6", {3.5, 3.9}, "Vibraphone"],
	  SoundNote["C2", {4., 4.4}, "Drums"],
	
	  SoundNote["C5", {4.5, 4.9}, "AMSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["D5", {5., 5.4}, "FMSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["E5", {5.5, 5.9}, "DuoSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["F4", {6., 6.4}, "MembraneSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["G5", {6.5, 6.9}, "MetalSynth"] (*WLJS only*)
	}]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["874f0eef-496c-4c85-b07a-36a970e76671"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKW5ibpBmkpqbpmliaJeuaJFuY6iYZmCfqGpslWpobpJqbmZkbAgCFlBVa"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

### A first procedural beat

The following 16-step groove is built from four independent layers: closed hi-hat, kick, snare, and an 808-style bass line. At 140 BPM, `step = 60/140/2` is one eighth-note step. Each layer is a list of time-stamped `SoundNote` objects; `Join` combines the layers into one `Sound`.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true" fade="true" >{`With[{step = 60/140/2},
	  Sound @ Join[
	    (*BB[*)(* closed hats *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    Table[
	      SoundNote["C6", {t, t + .035}, "MetalSynth"],
	      {t, 0, 15 step, step}
	    ],
	
	    (*BB[*)(* kick *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    {
	      SoundNote["C1", {0, .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {3 step, 3 step + .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {6 step, 6 step + .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {11 step, 11 step + .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {14 step, 14 step + .18}, "Drums"]
	    },
	
	    (*BB[*)(* snare / clap on beat 3 *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    {
	      SoundNote["C2", {4 step, 4 step + .12}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C2", {12 step, 12 step + .12}, "Drums"]
	    },
	
	    (*BB[*)(* sliding-feeling 808 bass line *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    {
	      SoundNote["C2", {0, 3 step}, "FMSynth"],
	      SoundNote["G1", {3 step, 4 step}, "FMSynth"],
	      SoundNote["Bb1", {6 step, 8 step}, "FMSynth"],
	      SoundNote["C2", {8 step, 11 step}, "FMSynth"],
	      SoundNote["Eb2", {12 step, 16 step}, "FMSynth"]
	    }
	  ]
	]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["c6e66bd4-10e6-4b9c-ad38-8bd62d23182f"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKJ5ulmpklpZjoGhqkmumaJFkm6yamGFvoWiSlmBmlGBkbWhilAQCL6hXV"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

## The `Music*` framework

WL 15 adds a higher-level symbolic layer for chords, notes, scores, voices, rests, and scales. Explore the available symbols with `Names["Music*"]`. These expressions are immutable and compositional: construct a musical object, inspect it, transform it, and combine it into a larger structure. We begin with a single chord:

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicChord["CMajor7"]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor>

### Inspecting a chord

Click the output to hear and inspect the chord. A chord can be queried for its constituent data; for example, extracting `"Bass"` returns a `MusicPitch` object.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]["Bass"]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`MusicPitch[(*VB[*) <|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNmYGAolgISTvkVbvlFuQmORUWJeempKcGlubmJRZVA4TRGkBp+IOFWlJ9X4pqXEpZZVFKamAOREEKScK1ITS4tSUzKSQ1WAQonJ1kYGiWlJOumWhgn6ZqYmFvoWpiaJ+smm5iZWFiapqVZJBulMYAMYQESPpnFJcWsINMSc4pTAbwfKnE="*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor>

Using a pitch and a duration object, you can construct a symbolic **note**.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicNote[MusicPitch[(*VB[*) <|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNmYGAolgISTvkVbvlFuQmORUWJeempKcGlubmJRZVA4TRGkBp+IOFWlJ9X4pqXEpZZVFKamAOREEKScK1ITS4tSUzKSQ1WAQonJ1kYGiWlJOumWhgn6ZqYmFvoWpiaJ+smm5iZWFiapqVZJBulMYAMYQESPpnFJcWsINMSc4pTAbwfKnE="*)(*]VB*)], MusicDuration[1/4]]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor>

By grouping notes and chords, you can construct a `MusicScore`. A score can contain multiple voices, rests, transformations, and metadata while remaining a single inspectable expression.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicScore[{
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>], "Name" -> "Major", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "D", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicTransform[MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)], {"Transpose", 7}],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>], "Name" -> "Major", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "A", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicRest[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxlkEFPAjEQhVfRRLhwNOGkh/0BbiRZuLEsjSYEk13FK4UOpkm3k8y2Uf690102Clxe533z0tf0cYvFvhdFUT1iyfBHIFWbGZG0X6BKX1WSDoz3VyEzZBGE1i2sWmtyXpp2ccPygkY1wwot/OGlrt2Zuw7u/l/fsefVQbXW8F0OeJd7kk6jnT60+cAWSjukEDmtbV2f5aNY5rBDBeUnuzhJ42Qmsnic8RknkwakT93EaN4txAVJn5uji45zcbylfVAoL7yB8i4MINWbNYeGvpOH+jb8lTQ1/AJZ8VKa"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/2|>], "Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "F", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]
	}]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["572c90bd-88cd-4175-ba26-b25edb2060f9"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/Ng3KFgIRbUX5eiWteimtFanJpSWJSTmqwClDY1Nwo2dIgKUXXwiI5RdfE0NxUNynRyEw3ycg0NSXJyMDMIM0SAJOJGIk="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

A great thing about WL's Music Framework is that it has all the necessary functions to transpose and invert chords out of the box. In the past, we had to build our own on top of `SoundNote`. Multiple voices can also be added using a `MusicVoice` container.

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`music = MusicScore[{
	 MusicVoice[{
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>], "Name" -> "Major", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "D", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "G", "MIDINumber" -> 67|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>], "Name" -> "Major", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "A", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicRest[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxlkEFPAjEQhVfRRLhwNOGkh/0BbiRZuLEsjSYEk13FK4UOpkm3k8y2Uf690102Clxe533z0tf0cYvFvhdFUT1iyfBHIFWbGZG0X6BKX1WSDoz3VyEzZBGE1i2sWmtyXpp2ccPygkY1wwot/OGlrt2Zuw7u/l/fsefVQbXW8F0OeJd7kk6jnT60+cAWSjukEDmtbV2f5aNY5rBDBeUnuzhJ42Qmsnic8RknkwakT93EaN4txAVJn5uji45zcbylfVAoL7yB8i4MINWbNYeGvpOH+jb8lTQ1/AJZ8VKa"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/2|>], "Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "F", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]
	 }],
	 
	 MusicVoice[{
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C", "MIDINumber" -> 48|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/2|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "D", "MIDINumber" -> 50|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "G", "MIDINumber" -> 55|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "A", "MIDINumber" -> 57|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicRest[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxlkM1LxDAQxesXqBePgif30D/AQqF6a+0GhWWFRrvXjWYqgTQD0wTd/95Ju8Wvy8u83zzyQhav2HRHSZIMVywVfgqkflsSKfcOWoa+V7Rj3B3EzAWLIHR+6XRryAdlp8UxywNaPQ5rdPCNV2bwf9xhdJc/+vY9jx761sCHPOddHUh5g+7uespHttTGI8XI79rJnbG8NKsa3lCD3LBLsyLNSlGlecVnmt2OoLiZJ0b380L8I0UxHnM0r8X+lulBsbwJFuRpHEDpJ2d3I32mAMNJ/CtlB/gCWwlSng=="*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Octave" -> 4, "Key" -> "D", "Name" -> "D"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "D", "MIDINumber" -> 38|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/2|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "D", "MIDINumber" -> 38|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]}, "Instrument"->"Organ"]
	}]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["2ba7e139-14c9-4ccc-83d0-e581995a1bf7"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/Ng3KFgIRbUX5eiWteimtFanJpSWJSTmqwClDYKCnRPNXQ2FLX0CTZUtckOTlZ18I4xUA31dTC0NLSNNEwKc0cAJUkGJE="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

Neat!

There is backward compatibility: you can wrap it in `Sound` and use it in `EmitSound`, for example:

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`EmitSound[music//Sound]`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`music//Sound`}</wljs-editor>

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["21d8180f-7712-41b3-89cc-792f44f2e99e"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKGxmmWBhaGKTpmpsbGumaGCYZ61pYJifrmlsapZmYpBmlWlqmAgB0VxUn"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor>

If you need scales, there is a special symbol for that:

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicScale@RandomChoice@MusicScale["Names"]`}</wljs-editor>

Construct chords by sampling every third pitch in the list:

<wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`pitches = MusicScale[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Lydian Augmented"|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]["PitchList"];
	pitches = 
	  Join[pitches, 
	   MusicTransform[{"Transpose", 12}] /@ Rest@pitches];
	
	Table[MusicChord@pitches[[{i, i + 2, i + 4, i + 6}]], {i, 4}]//TableForm`}</wljs-editor>
